title: MCP Reliability, Cancellation, and Flow Control

questions.question: A mutation response is lost and the client retries with a new JSON-RPC id. What makes the retry safe?
options: The new JSON-RPC id automatically deduplicates the mutation
The tool descriptor includes an idempotentHint
A durable application idempotency key reused with identical arguments
The retry uses the same HTTP connection
questions.explanation: JSON-RPC ids correlate messages. Business idempotency requires a durable key, an argument fingerprint, and a stored committed result.

questions.question: How does a client cancel an in-flight request over stdio in MCP 2026-07-28?
options: Call tasks/cancel for the JSON-RPC id
Send notifications/cancelled with the active request id
Close a per-request SSE stream
Send a DELETE request to the MCP endpoint
questions.explanation: stdio has no per-request response stream, so the client sends the fire-and-forget notifications/cancelled notification.

questions.question: How does a client cancel an in-flight Streamable HTTP request?
options: Close that request's SSE response stream
POST notifications/cancelled to the MCP endpoint
Wait for the server to send notifications/cancelled
Send Last-Event-ID with an empty value
questions.explanation: For modern Streamable HTTP, closing the request-specific response stream is the cancellation signal.

questions.question: Progress keeps arriving before every idle timeout. Which deadline must still end a runaway request?
options: An absolute maximum timeout measured from request start
The next pagination cursor expiry
The proxy keepalive interval
The Task polling interval
questions.explanation: Valid progress may reset the idle clock, but an absolute maximum deadline must remain in force.

questions.question: What does a successful tasks/cancel response prove?
options: The durable result was deleted
The worker has already stopped
The server acknowledged cancellation intent
The Task must eventually become cancelled
questions.explanation: Task cancellation is cooperative. The Task may remain working, finish first, or reach cancelled after a worker checkpoint.

questions.question: A subscription SSE stream drops after several progress events. Which recovery plan fits MCP 2026-07-28?
options: Resume from Last-Event-ID and replay every in-flight mutation
Open a GET event stream and restore Mcp-Session-Id
Keep the old request id and assume no updates were lost
Open a new listen request, refetch authoritative state, and avoid unsafe mutation replay
questions.explanation: Modern MCP streams are not resumable with Last-Event-ID. Recovery uses a new request plus authoritative refetch and explicit retry safety.
